SUPPORT US! GET MICROSLOP: https://store.gamersnexus.net/products/microslop-parody-t-shirt or grab one of our DATA DRAGNET campaign supporter packs! https://store.gamersnexus.net/data-dragnet
We estimate 25,000,000 to 35,000,000 ASUS routers -- nearly every modern router the company has sold since 2018 -- are affected by vulnerabilities discovered by security researcher Mr Bruh. Working with Mr Bruh, we've exploit chained the ASUS vulnerability into the unpatched LG TV remote code execution vulnerabilities, enabling us to breach and take over an ASUS router to then tunnel into a TV and convert it into a listening device. This could be easily done, for example, from an office lobby, cafe, or business with available WiFi networks or open wall sockets. Likewise, you could chain in from a more remote position by exploiting other device vulnerabilities. ASUS' response was lackluster, as it often is, and the company requested an extension on its fixes.

articles.content:
Grab a MICROSLOP T-SHIRT! https://store.gamersnexus.net/products/microslop-parody-t-shirt
Micron has discovered an infinite money glitch: Just keep increasing the price, or something. It was that simple all along. Micron's consumer margin is now a disgusting 90%, multiplying what they make versus prior quarters. That's in spite of the company killing Crucial in December of last year, which was its direct-to-consumer line of system components. The company still has consumer parts, but seeing them continue to skyrocket in margin and price after cutting Crucial tells us just how much money these companies are making. In its latest earnings report, Micron noted that it expects the "shortage" to continue into 2027 and 2028 at least, with several of its customers -- like the big AI hyperscalers -- wanting contract extensions beyond 2030.

articles.content:
SUPPORT OUR WORK: https://store.gamersnexus.net/data-dragnet for the campaign, or grab individual items here: https://store.gamersnexus.net/
The AI companies all gathered together to collectively write a new so-called "AI Constitution" where they police themselves. The accord effectively does nothing, but it does set in place the pieces to enable what should be competitors to collaborate even closer. In addition to a rebranding as "Super Intelligence" with an Executive Order, AI has faced increasing calls for regulation from the public while executives like Jensen Huang of NVIDIA have demanded speeding-up development. Jensen's cousin, Lisa Su of AMD, has partnered with Michael Kratsios of the White House to reduce clean air and clean water regulations that slow data center buildouts. They've already had the same goals, it seems -- but now the companies are formalizing a partnership.

In their examples, singleplayer costs more than training mode, but multiplayer costs
articles.content:
SUPPORT OUR WORK https://store.gamersnexus.net/data-dragnet
Microsoft has filed for a new patent that describes a credit system to "rent" software and games, including rate-limited rentals based on the type of use. In their examples, singleplayer costs more than training mode, but multiplayer costs more credits than both. Users can 'earn' credits by subjecting themselves to more advertisements during loading screens, round win or loss screens, and level loading screens. The patent technology can be applied at the application level, OS level, and device level, making it wide-reaching and affecting more than just Windows machines. In one instance, Microsoft explicitly names Smart TVs. This would be similar, in some ways, to ACR (Automatic Content Recognition) on LG or other Smart TVs, where the patent-pending technology could scan the screen and audio.

articles.author: Gamers Nexus
articles.summary: Sponsor: Thermal Grizzly Duronaut on Amazon - https://geni.us/tpgcPMw The cyclical nature of memory manufacturing may finally be broken -- and not in a good way for consumers. The memory manufacturers have all moved toward long-term agreements with longer terms and capacity than previously, with Mic
articles.content:
Sponsor: Thermal Grizzly Duronaut on Amazon - https://geni.us/tpgcPMw
The cyclical nature of memory manufacturing may finally be broken -- and not in a good way for consumers. The memory manufacturers have all moved toward long-term agreements with longer terms and capacity than previously, with Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix diverting a flood of memory away from consumers. At the same time, Amazon has publicly stated that more users than ever will consider its cloud services due to the rising costs of on-location hardware. But don't worry: By 2035, Micron will save us all.

articles.title: NVIDIA Has GPUs If You Have Coin
articles.author: Gamers Nexus
articles.summary: Sponsor: Thermal Grizzly Duronaut on Amazon - https://geni.us/tpgcPMw GPU prices have become a meme, with NVIDIA leading the pack at (on average) 70% over listed MSRP for its consumer and gaming video cards. AMD and Intel are likewise running higher prices than previously, reaching new highs for GPU
articles.content:
Sponsor: Thermal Grizzly Duronaut on Amazon - https://geni.us/tpgcPMw
GPU prices have become a meme, with NVIDIA leading the pack at (on average) 70% over listed MSRP for its consumer and gaming video cards. AMD and Intel are likewise running higher prices than previously, reaching new highs for GPU prices in our year-long series tracking them. November of 2025 seems like it was the best time to buy, with prices now climbing even past what we saw in February of 2026. This continues to get worse with thanks to the ongoing DRAM availability crisis thanks to AI data center buildout -- one largely caused by the very companies that make the consumer GPUs.
